display.title: Episode 220: The Rambam's Grave, Chapter 1
display.summary_short: Just before Rosh Chodesh Nissan: news of the Pesach Experience, the life of the Rambam and the mystery of where he should be buried, more 'My Sefer Torah' entries, and children leading the way to Moshiach.
display.summary_long: Broadcast two days before Rosh Chodesh Nissan. Uncle Yossi announces the Tzivos Hashem 'Pesach Experience' for Chol HaMoed, with acrobatics, a children's music show and a siyum on the Rambam's Sefer HaMitzvos in honor of the Rambam's birthday on Erev Pesach. After the Hakochainik march he explains the name Rambam, and a young yeshiva student recites the Shema. The story begins the life of the Rambam: born in Cordova on Erev Pesach, forced to flee with his family as a boy, wandering to Morocco, surviving a storm at sea through prayer, praying at the Kosel and the Me'aras HaMachpelah, and settling in Egypt, where he wrote the Thirteen Principles of Faith, the Mishneh Torah and the Moreh Nevuchim. When he passed away he asked to be buried in Eretz Yisroel without saying where, and the people of Yerushalayim, Chevron and Meron each claimed the honor; a mystery awaits at the border. After a sponsor message come the Pesach matzah ball contest and a reading of contest entries, including a child's poem about loving Torah. The show closes with the teaching that just as children led the way out of Egypt, children will lead the way when Moshiach comes.
display.lesson: Like the children who led the way out of Egypt, Jewish children will lead the way to Moshiach, so bring your friends closer to Torah and mitzvos.

date.note: 'Rosh Chodesh Nissan... this coming Thursday, April the 10th'; the Pesach Experience is on 'Sunday, April 27, the second day of Chol HaMoed'. Matches the weekly estimate.

advisories.note: The Rambam's family is forced to flee Cordova and wander for years because they could not live as Jews.
The Rambam's passing and the question of his burial place.

privacy.note: Shema guest and many contest entrants named in full, some with home towns.

characters: representatives of Yerushalayim, Chevron and Meron

sources_cited.note: 'From Moshe until Moshe there arose none like Moshe' said of the Rambam.
At the Splitting of the Sea, the children were the first to recognize Hashem ('hem hikiru techilah'); cited as 'our Chachamim tell us'.
